steps.text: Combine sugar, cornstarch, and salt in a 2-quart saucepan. Slowly stir in milk and bring to a boil. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes more. Stir in vanilla.
Pour hot pudding into dessert glasses or molds that have been rinsed in cold water. Chill until firm, at least 2 hours. Unmold if desired and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Pudding from Scratch
raw_recipe.description: Make this pudding from scratch with basic pantry ingredients, and you'll never want to buy a boxed pudding mix again. It's easy and so delicious!
raw_recipe.name: Pudding from Scratch

review.reviewBody: I've made this about 8 times now... I've done different flavors and had great success. Used brown sugar instead of white for a butterscotchy flavor, added lemon extract and zest for lemon pudding, and added chocolate chips for choccy pudding. Tonight I made choccy and put it in a baked pie crust and topped with whipped cream... 3 adults and 2 kids finished it off in 1 sitting.

I added a tablespoon of cocoa powder, a teaspoon of instant coffee, and 1/2 a teaspoon of cinnamon, and it was delicious. It's a great recipe even without my editions.
Thank you.
Very easy recipe, I added I egg to the last 1/2 cup of milk (beaten well) gradually added to the mix before it was too hot. Nice rich flavor!

I didn't make any changes to the ingred. but I did cook the pudding in the microwave! I put all ingred. in a very large bowl, whisked it, then set the timer for 2 minutes. I stirred every minute after, until the pudding was thick. I was more than happy with my creamy, easy, homemade pudding!
YUM, now that's comfort food!

I've been searching for a way to make a coconut cream pie filling without all the egg,as I have egg allergies, and this was wonderful. It made the perfect creamy filling. I did make modifications. I used coconut palm sugar instead of regular sugar. I used 1 cup of coconut cream and 1.5 cups of whole milk to = the 2.5 cups of milk it called for. I ended up leaving out the vanilla and adding natural coconut extract. It turned out nice a creamy and the perfect consistency.Thanks!I'll be trying this recipe with different flavorings.

I opted to go the vegan route as I intend to share with a coworker that's vegan. I used plant based whipping cream instead of milk, I added in about 1/4 cup of liquid from thawed frozen bananas, 2 thawed bananas, an extra tablespoon of corn starch, and an extra tablespoon of sugar to the mix along with 1/2 tablespoon more of vanilla extract. I tasted a small spillover and I must say, you can't even tell it's plant based and it tastes amazing!

This was as simple as it could be. I see other reviews about people having lumpy or runny textures... Mine turned out perfectly! Perhaps people haven't made pudding before and don't realize you have to continuously stir it. This is a great recipe. The only change I made was cutting down the sugar to 1/4c and adding 2T of cacao powder to make it chocolate flavoured. Muy bien!

My husband recently had 2 teeth pulled so I made this for him. I added 1 1/2 cup nestle chocolate chips right before I took it off the heat. It was really good and he devoured it fast. Will need to triple the recipe next time.
I love this recipe! Simple but delicious...the only changes I made were to increase the sugar to 1/2 cup, and add some cinnamon...

I’ve never made pudding from scratch before, it was really easy. I put it in little dessert cups which yielded 6 servings but one of these cups was more than enough. I don’t like anything too sweet so I felt 1/3 cup was too sweet for me. I will definitely make again and maybe use less sugar. Thanks for the recipe!

This is an excellent pudding. It's way better than any packaged mix, most of which will start to separate after a day or two. This (at least what was left) was still in fine shape three days later. I made this for dirt pudding for our senior center lunch on Wednesday - yeah with the gummy worms and flowers "growing" out of the "dirt". Great consistency - an excellent pudding to which you can add fruit or eat by itself. I made it with 2% milk and was generous with the vanilla extract. I also replaced 2/3 of the sugar requirement with store brand of Splenda to accommodate the diabetics. Everyone enjoyed the custard. Oh, I also took the suggestion of one of the other reviewers to add a bit of food coloring - great idea - white custard just doesn't have the same appeal as one with a bit of color. Thanks to the recipe poster - this is a winner!
Simple ingredients, directions easy to follow. You cant mess this up. Tastes like the good ole days! Why would you ever use boxed pudding again? Thanks for sharing.
This is a great recipe! The only change I made was that I added 2 1/2 tablespoons of vanilla, because I love an intense vanilla flavor. It was fabulous!

Love to make this, so easy to make and really hits the spot.

I had tried it with real strawberries and it was awesome.

1/6 cup sugar
1-1/2 tbsp cornstarch
1-1/4 cup milk
Flavor - instead of 1 tsp vanilla extract, used a large lemon thinly sliced since really in the mood for sweet and sour
Whipped up and warmed up until thick
Very easy recipe. Like the variety of suggestions for flavours too. Will definitely make again.
The kids and I loved this! Added some chocolate chips and it was great!
This is my first time making a pudding, and this this recipe is REALLY GREAT!! I looooove the taste! i will definitely make this again next time with double recipe ;)
Flavor was not great even after I added double the vanilla. It just tastes sweet...
This recipe was exactly what I was looking for!
